title: OUTPUT contract (_passthrough_columns) ignores the fields-based select for non-terminal output nodes
description: output_fn narrows its frame to config['fields'] (`if fields: lf = lf.select(fields)`), but OUTPUT is registered with _passthrough_columns (reads nothing, produces nothing => models full pass-through). The projection layer compensates only when the OUTPUT node is TERMINAL: projection.py:2166-2168 seeds `needed` from fields for childless OUTPUT nodes. For a non-terminal OUTPUT (one that has downstream children), the special case does not apply and the contract claims pass-through; the planner therefore propagates child demand through unchanged, but the runtime select(fields) drops any demanded column not in `fields`, causing a downstream column-not-found. This is a latent gap that only manifests for the unusual topology of an OUTPUT node feeding further nodes; if such topologies are intentionally rejected elsewhere this is moot, but the contract/runtime divergence is concrete and unguarded.
evidence: output_fn l.753-755 selects fields; registration l.743 uses columns=_passthrough_columns; projection.py terminal-only fields seeding at l.2165-2168 (guarded by `if not children`). No fields handling for non-terminal OUTPUT.
